analysis:
Compared both scanner and diagnostics revisions, metadata, and all supplied workflow hunks. budget_scan.py:303-326,332,367 now plans source/depth workloads and each integration round through an optional adapter hook; citation validation, cache identity, finding retention, escalation and convergence checks remain intact. Workflow lines 128-137 increase native workload/output allowances and establish a 3000-second scan timeout within a 60-minute job. These are intentional capacity changes, not independently demonstrated billing bypasses. Integration must inspect the native adapter's plan_calls/reservation logic, cumulative 500-call ceiling, cache-hit accounting and single repair-call allowance, plus timeout enforcement; those controls are outside this batch.
The workflow removes paid manual dispatch and its PR resolver, retains pull_request_target review and explicit fork opt-in for AWS (lines 63-73), and keeps trusted-scanner checkout in visible surrounding context. No newly introduced execution of PR source or interpolation of attacker text is evident in these hunks. Full authentication/workflow setup is not supplied.
budget_scan.py:400 sets finished even after caught failures, while errors, incomplete coverage and pending depth remain recorded. Check downstream report/clearance consumers interpret finished as terminal execution rather than successful clearance. diagnostics.py:82-83 exports this status and four adapter policy/count fields; no source, credential or prompt fields are newly exported, but integration should verify those adapter metrics contain only bounded policy labels/numbers.
No supported regression directly affects the canonical provider assets or TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-009/TB-010/TB-011 controls, including T-008 encryption, T-041 cache isolation, and T-053 authorization freshness: this batch changes review infrastructure, not serving behavior. The compact index and selected T-041 detail were considered, not every definition's full text. Remaining uncertainty concerns cross-file cost enforcement and clearance semantics, not evidence of an observed vulnerability.
